GPT-5.5 "Spud" and Claude Mythos 5: The Next Frontier Models Are in the Works

By Will Zheng · April 6, 2026 · From Issue #5

OpenAI / PrimeAI Center / Mean.CEO Industry

OpenAI's next model, GPT-5.5 (internally codenamed "Spud"), completed pretraining around March 24. CEO Sam Altman described a release timeline of "a few weeks" and framed it as a macro-economic inflection point rather than an incremental update; CTO Greg Brockman called it the product of two years of research. It is being trained at Stargate scale — the five new Stargate data center sites announced this week collectively bring planned network capacity to approximately 7 gigawatts and $400B+ in committed investment. On the Anthropic side, a data leak surfaced an internal reference to "Claude Mythos 5" — reportedly a 10-trillion-parameter model described as a "step change" beyond Claude Opus, currently in early access with cybersecurity and coding partners. Anthropic has not officially confirmed the name, parameter count, or release timeline. Both stories matter less for what they tell us today and more for what they signal: the labs are not slowing down, the race is accelerating, and the enterprise gap between frontier capability and actual deployment is widening.
